why.matters: Content accumulates. Usage and lineage tell you what to invest in, what to fix first and what to retire safely.
why.failure: A "clean-up" deletes a model with no report views; the monthly commission paginated report that depended on it fails on payroll day.
why.use: Usage metrics and activity events for what's used, lineage and impact analysis for what depends on what, capacity metrics for cost, and a retirement process with notice and a read-only period.
why.avoid: Deleting based on view counts alone.

verified.context: Usage metrics, lineage/impact analysis, Capacity Metrics app docs (Microsoft Learn, Sept 2026)

asg.brief: From the mock activity events, list the reports nobody viewed in 90 days and the most-viewed one, then say what you must check before retiring any of them.
req: Unused reports from the activity data.
The most-viewed report and its views.
The checks before retirement (lineage, subscriptions, paginated reports, Excel connections, owners).

Before retiring: impact analysis, subscriptions, dashboard tiles, Analyze in Excel connections, owner contact, then read-only for 30 days.

asg.t: What should a BI monitoring page show?
asg.brief: Design one page Elena can check every Monday that shows the health of the estate. Choose at most eight numbers and justify each.
req: Refresh, usage, capacity, ownership and quality signals.
Which numbers have thresholds and who acts on them.
asg.exp: For example: failed refreshes (7 days), certified-model refresh duration trend, capacity peak utilisation and throttling, views on certified vs uncertified content, items without owner, retirement candidates, data-quality test failures, open incidents. Each with an owner and a threshold.

asg.brief: Write the retirement runbook your team will use, based on the Regional Sales Weekly drill (D05).
req: What makes you stop and roll back.
asg.exp: Check dependencies → notify owner and recent viewers → banner and move subscriptions/tiles → read-only 30 days → archive → delete after 90 days; stop if a dependency or an objection appears; restore from archive if needed.

int.q: What's the difference between usage metrics and activity events?
int.a: Usage metrics reports show views and viewers for content in a workspace. Activity events (admin API or audit log) record what every user did across the tenant (views, exports, shares, edits), which is what you need for tenant-wide analysis and audits.

Downstream items that depend on an item (reports, dashboards, other models, dataflows) across workspaces, and how many people use them, so you can notify owners before a breaking change or retirement.

int.q: Why can a model with zero report views still be important?
int.a: It may feed paginated reports, subscriptions, composite models, Analyze in Excel workbooks or other tools that usage metrics for reports don't capture.

int.q: What does the Capacity Metrics app tell you?
int.a: How much of the capacity each item and operation uses over time, interactive vs background, and when throttling happens: the evidence for optimising or resizing.

ass.q: A model has no report views in 90 days. Before deleting it you should check:
o: Lineage/impact analysis, subscriptions, paginated reports and Excel connections, and ask the owner
ass.why: Views on reports aren't the only way content is used.
